result.texto: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE WEG selects TURBOdesign Suite for leveraging the Hydraulic Turbine Design process, substantially improving its speed and efficiency. Advanced Design Technology (ADT), a global leader in turbomachinery design software, and WEG, global electro-electronic equipment company, have joined forces to streamline and optimize the design process for hydraulic turbines. Aiming to bolster their capabilities in energy efficiency, WEG’s hydraulic design team sought a sophisticated tool to design and optimize hydraulic turbines for both new and refurbishment projects. After extensive research, WEG identified ADT’s TURBOdesign Suite as the optimal solution due to its unique 3D Inverse Design approach and the ability to quickly generate new blade profiles with specific characteristics for each project. "The integration within the existing CAE environment was seamless, TURBOdesign export geometries in point, surface or solid formats for all major CAD, CFD and FEA software, it also links directly to CFD and Optimization codes allowing full stage optimization even for multiple operating conditions", said Andre Eger. "We are excited to partner with ADT as we anticipate a significant return on investment within the first year of software usage, thanks to the considerable reduction in manual work, accelerated design process and associated cost savings." “Hydropower plays a crucial role in the current energy generation landscape by providing a reliable, renewable, and low-emission source of electricity that supports grid stability and reduces dependence on fossil fuels”, said Prof. Mehrdad Zangeneh, Managing Director of ADT and Professor of Thermofluids at University College London (UCL). “TURBOdesign has a critical role in supporting development of high efficiency and cavitation free designs across all types of hydraulic turbines.” This collaboration between WEG and ADT marks a significant step towards revolutionizing hydraulic turbine design and optimizing energy efficiency, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable and innovative future. For more information on the case study and the partnership between ADT and WEG, please visit our website or contact the press contact below. About Advanced Design Technology Ltd. Advanced Design Technology (ADT) is a global leader in the development of advanced turbomachinery design methods, which help shorten development time and improve performance of turbomachinery components. Our aim is to put designers in direct control of the aerodynamic design and to considerably shorten the design time and time to market for a range of turbomachinery products. ADT’s clients, who represent some of the leading global players in the aerospace, automotive, power generation and marine fields, have achieved significant returns on investment in terms of reduction in design times, higher performance and ease of know-how transfer among different design teams and projects. For more information, call +44 (0) 20 7299 1170 or go to: www.adtechnology.com About WEG WEG was founded in 1961 and is a global electro-electronic equipment company, operating in the capital goods sector with focus on electric motors, gearboxes and drives and controls, energy generation and transformers, electrification products and systems, automation and digitalization and Liquid and Powder Coatings. WEG stands out in innovation by constantly developing solutions to meet the major trends in energy efficiency, renewable energy and electric mobility. www.weg.net Media Contacts Ali Panchoo Advanced Design Technology +44 (0) 20 7299 1170 a.panchoo@adtechnology.com

During the meeting, Thieren said organizations discussed how important it would be to scientifically demonstrate the occurrence of a famine in Gaza, and how to use the term for communication and political pressure on Israel. According to him, this was explicitly discussed at the highest levels in these meetings.“At the very end of the meeting – I won’t say exactly where, and it wasn’t necessarily at the WHO, rest assured – there was a gathering of experts who asked the question quite forcefully.
